title: Best Starbucks Drink for a Hangover: What to Order (and Skip)
excerpt: The best Starbucks drinks for a hangover, ranked by what's bothering you: headache, nausea, or exhaustion. Caffeine amounts, the Medicine Ball, food picks, and what to skip.
metaDescription: The best Starbucks drink for a hangover: what to order for a headache or nausea, caffeine amounts, the Medicine Ball, food picks, and what to skip.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest answer first:** the best Starbucks drink for a hangover is usually a modest amount of caffeine plus something gentle on your stomach, ordered alongside a large cup of water. For most people that means a tall or short latte (or a tall brewed coffee if your stomach can take it), a free cup of ice water, and some food such as egg bites or oatmeal. If your stomach is upset, a caffeine-free herbal tea like Mint Majesty or the Honey Citrus Mint Tea (the drink people call the "Medicine Ball") is the kinder pick. No Starbucks drink cures a hangover. The menu can help with three specific problems: the caffeine-withdrawal headache if you're a daily coffee drinker, mild nausea, and getting fluid and food into you when you don't feel like cooking.

**The quick order guide:**

- **Pounding head, daily coffee drinker:** tall latte or tall Pike Place, plus a venti ice water.
- **Queasy stomach:** Mint Majesty or Peach Tranquility herbal tea, or a Honey Citrus Mint Tea with less honey.
- **Wiped out but stomach is fine:** a tall cold brew or an Americano, plus egg bites.
- **Can't face anything hot or bitter:** a Refresher or an iced tea, unsweetened if you can manage it, plus water.
- **Skip for now:** venti brewed coffee, Frappuccinos loaded with syrup and whipped cream, and anything with extra espresso shots.

> **Feeling worse than a normal hangover?** A hangover is unpleasant, but it shouldn't be scary. **Get medical help right away** if you or a friend can't keep any fluids down for several hours, are vomiting repeatedly, are confused or very hard to wake, have a seizure, have chest pain or a racing heartbeat that won't settle, have slow or irregular breathing, or have cold, clammy, or bluish skin. Those can be signs of alcohol poisoning or severe dehydration, not a hangover. In the US, call 911. And if you get shaky, sweaty, anxious, or sick whenever you go a day without drinking, that's worth raising with a doctor, because those can be withdrawal symptoms rather than an ordinary hangover.

## Why Starbucks Can Help a Hangover (and Where It Can't)

A hangover isn't one problem. It's a bundle of them: dehydration from alcohol's effect on your kidneys, poor-quality sleep, irritation of your stomach lining, low-grade inflammation, a dip in blood sugar for some people, and the leftover effects of acetaldehyde, the toxic by-product your liver makes when it breaks down alcohol. Researchers still argue about which of these matters most, and the honest summary is that nothing on any coffee shop menu fixes the whole bundle.

What a Starbucks run *can* do is help with a few of the pieces:

1. **It can stop a caffeine-withdrawal headache.** If you normally drink coffee every morning and you slept in, part of your headache may be caffeine withdrawal stacked on top of the hangover. That part responds well to caffeine. This is probably the main reason so many people swear coffee helps.
2. **It can make you feel more alert.** Caffeine blocks adenosine, a chemical that builds up and makes you feel sleepy. After a night of broken sleep, that lift is real, even though it doesn't fix the underlying tiredness.
3. **It gets fluid and food into you.** Water is free, and the food case has easy, bland options. Eating something and drinking fluid are two of the few hangover habits with broad agreement behind them.

What it can't do: caffeine doesn't speed up how fast your liver clears alcohol or acetaldehyde, it doesn't rehydrate you better than water, and it won't sober you up if there's still alcohol in your blood. Coffee can make you feel more awake while you're still impaired, which is the dangerous part. If you were drinking late, don't let a latte convince you that you're fine to drive.

For a deeper look at the research on coffee itself, see our full guide to [coffee for a hangover](/never-hungover/coffee-for-hangover).

## The Best Starbucks Drinks for a Hangover, Ranked by Situation

Below are the drinks worth ordering, grouped by what's actually bothering you. Caffeine figures are approximate and based on what Starbucks has published for US grande (16 oz) sizes. Recipes and numbers change and vary by region, so check the Starbucks app or the in-store nutrition info if the exact amount matters to you.

### 1. A tall or short latte (best all-rounder)

A latte is espresso with a lot of steamed milk. For a hangover, that combination works well. You get a moderate dose of caffeine (a grande latte has two espresso shots, roughly 150 mg; a tall has one, around 75 mg), and the milk softens the acidity and bitterness that can make a sore stomach worse. Milk also adds a little protein and fluid.

**Why it works:** enough caffeine to head off a withdrawal headache without the jitters, and gentler on the stomach than black coffee.

**How to order it:** a tall latte with whole, 2%, or oat milk. Skip extra shots. If you want sweetness, one or two pumps of syrup is plenty. A lot more sugar can leave you feeling worse an hour later.

**Skip it if:** dairy upsets your stomach. Ask for oat, almond, soy, or coconut milk instead.

### 2. Tall brewed coffee or Americano (if your stomach is fine)

Starbucks brewed coffee is strong. A grande Pike Place has been listed at around 310 mg of caffeine, and the Blonde Roast is even higher. That's close to the 400 mg a day that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) describes as an amount not generally linked to harmful effects in healthy adults. Drink a venti on a hangover and you've nearly used up a whole day's worth in one cup, at a time when your heart may already be beating faster than normal.

**Why it works:** quick, cheap, and effective if you're a regular coffee drinker who needs your usual dose.

**How to order it:** a tall (12 oz), not a grande or venti. An Americano (espresso topped with hot water) gives you more control. A tall has two shots, a grande three. Add a splash of milk if the acidity bothers you.

**Skip it if:** you're nauseous, you have heartburn, or your heart already feels jumpy. Black coffee is acidic and can make all three worse.

### 3. Cold brew (smoother, but still strong)

Cold brew is steeped in cold water for many hours. People often find it smoother and less bitter than hot brewed coffee, which can help when your stomach is touchy. A grande cold brew has been listed at roughly 205 mg of caffeine, and the nitro version is higher.

**Why it works:** many people find it easier to drink cold when they feel overheated or sweaty, and you can sip it slowly.

**How to order it:** a tall cold brew with a splash of milk. The sweet cream versions add a lot of sugar and fat. That's fine if it's what you can face, but not ideal if you're queasy.

### 4. Mint Majesty or Peach Tranquility herbal tea (best for nausea)

These are caffeine-free herbal teas on the Starbucks menu. Mint Majesty is a blend of spearmint and peppermint. Peach Tranquility is a fruity herbal blend. Neither contains black or green tea leaves, so you get a warm drink and fluid with no caffeine at all.

**Why it works:** peppermint is a traditional remedy for an upset stomach, and some people find the smell alone settles nausea. The evidence for peppermint helping hangover nausea specifically is thin, but it's a gentle, low-risk drink, and warm fluids are easy to sip slowly. If nausea is your main problem, our [hangover nausea guide](/never-hungover/hangover-nausea-complete-guide-fast-stomach-relief-2025) covers what else helps.

**How to order it:** a tall or grande hot tea. Ask for a little honey on the side if you want something sweet.

### 5. Honey Citrus Mint Tea, the "Medicine Ball" (comforting, but sugary)

This drink started as a "secret menu" order that customers called the Medicine Ball, and Starbucks later added it to the regular menu as the Honey Citrus Mint Tea. It combines a green tea blended with mint and lemon verbena (Jade Citrus Mint), the Peach Tranquility herbal tea, hot water, steamed lemonade, and honey.

**Why people like it:** it's warm, soothing, and tastes like something your grandmother would make for a cold. The green tea adds a small amount of caffeine, much less than coffee. The honey and lemonade give you some quick sugar, which can help if you're shaky and haven't eaten.

**The catch:** it's fairly high in sugar because of the lemonade and honey. Some sugar is fine on a hangover morning, but a big sugary drink on an empty stomach can lead to a crash later. There's also no good evidence that it does anything special for a hangover beyond being warm, comforting, and wet.

**How to order it:** a tall, and ask for less honey (or "light lemonade") if you want to cut the sugar. If you'd rather avoid caffeine entirely, ask for it made with Peach Tranquility and Mint Majesty instead of the green tea.

### 6. Matcha latte or chai latte (gentler caffeine)

A grande matcha latte has been listed at roughly 80 mg of caffeine and a grande chai latte at roughly 95 mg. That's well below brewed coffee, so these are good middle-ground options when you want a little lift without a full coffee dose.

**Why it works:** moderate caffeine, milk for your stomach, and ginger-and-spice notes in the chai that some people find soothing.

**The catch:** both are pre-sweetened at Starbucks, and you can't fully remove the sweetness. Ask for fewer pumps of chai concentrate (or matcha with less sweetener, where available) if sugar bothers you.

### 7. Refreshers and iced tea (if you want something cold and light)

Starbucks Refreshers, such as the Strawberry Açaí and its lemonade or coconut milk version, the Pink Drink, contain green coffee extract. A grande has been listed at roughly 45 mg of caffeine. Iced black, green, and passion tango teas are also options, and the Passion Tango (a hibiscus herbal tea) is caffeine-free.

**Why it works:** cold, mostly water, easy to drink, and lighter on caffeine. If the thought of a hot coffee makes you queasy, this is a reasonable way to get fluid in.

**How to order it:** ask for the iced tea unsweetened, or with light classic syrup. Refreshers are already sweetened. A tall is plenty.

## What Not to Order on a Hangover

Some drinks are fine on a normal day but a poor fit for a hangover morning.

- **Venti brewed coffee or extra espresso shots.** Big caffeine loads can make anxiety, shakiness, and a racing heart worse. Many people already feel jittery and anxious the morning after drinking, sometimes called "hangxiety," and loading on caffeine can push that further.
- **Large Frappuccinos with extra syrup and whipped cream.** They're mostly sugar and fat. Some people find a rich, cold treat comforting, and that's fine as a choice. But if you're nauseous, a heavy, very sweet drink is more likely to come back up than settle.
- **Anything acidic and black if you have heartburn.** Alcohol relaxes the valve at the top of your stomach and irritates the stomach lining, so heartburn the next morning is common. Black coffee and citrus can add to it.
- **Nothing but coffee.** The mistake isn't ordering a coffee. It's ordering only a coffee and calling that breakfast.

## Does Coffee Dehydrate You When You're Hungover?

This is one of the most common worries, and the answer is better than most people expect. Caffeine does have a mild diuretic effect, meaning it can make you pee a bit more. But in regular coffee drinkers the effect is small, because the body builds tolerance. Research on habitual coffee drinkers has generally found that moderate coffee intake contributes to daily fluid needs rather than working against them.

Alcohol is the much bigger problem. It suppresses vasopressin, a hormone that tells your kidneys to hold onto water, so you lose more fluid than you drink while you're out. Our guide on [whether alcohol dehydrates you](/never-hungover/does-alcohol-dehydrate-you) explains how that works.

So a moderate coffee won't make your dehydration meaningfully worse. It also won't fix it. Plain water does that job better, which is why the free cup of ice water is the most useful thing you can ask for at the counter. Ask for a venti water with your drink and finish it before you leave.

If you were sick or sweated a lot, water alone may not replace the salt and potassium you lost. An electrolyte drink can help in that case. Our [electrolyte drink comparison](/never-hungover/electrolyte-drinks-for-hangover-compared) covers the options.

## The Best Starbucks Food for a Hangover

Food matters at least as much as the drink. Eating gives your body some steady energy, helps if your blood sugar is low, and gives your stomach something besides coffee to deal with. Starbucks food menus change often and vary by country, but these types of items are usually available.

| Item type | Why it can help | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| Egg bites | Protein, soft texture, easy on a sore stomach | Some versions are fairly salty |
| Rolled oats / oatmeal | Bland, warm, slow-release carbohydrates | Toppings add sugar; go light |
| Breakfast sandwiches or wraps | Protein, carbs, and some fat to keep you full | Heavy, greasy ones may not sit well if you're nauseous |
| Plain bagel or toast-style items | Bland carbs when your stomach can't handle much | Not very filling on their own |
| Bananas (where sold) | Easy to eat, some potassium | Not much protein |
| Protein boxes | Eggs, cheese, fruit, and crackers in small portions | Fine to pick at slowly |

Eggs come up a lot in hangover advice. They contain cysteine, an amino acid your body uses to make glutathione, an antioxidant involved in processing acetaldehyde. That's a plausible reason to eat them, though there is no good evidence that eating eggs measurably shortens a hangover. We cover this in detail in [eggs for a hangover](/never-hungover/eggs-for-hangover).

For more ideas once you're home, see our [best hangover breakfast guide](/never-hungover/best-hangover-breakfast).

## How Much Caffeine Is Too Much on a Hangover?

A good rule is to drink about as much caffeine as you normally do, not more. Here's why.

- **If you drink coffee every day,** your usual amount prevents a withdrawal headache. Going over it gives you little extra benefit and more chance of jitters.
- **If you rarely drink coffee,** a hangover morning is not the time to start with a grande brewed coffee. A small latte, a chai, or a matcha is a gentler way in, or skip caffeine altogether and stick with herbal tea and water.
- **If your heart is already racing,** hold off on caffeine. A fast heartbeat is common after drinking, and caffeine can add to it. If your heart is pounding, irregular, or comes with chest pain or shortness of breath, that's a reason to get checked rather than to order a smaller coffee.

Keep in mind that the FDA's general figure of about 400 mg a day for healthy adults is a ceiling, not a target. People who are pregnant, have heart rhythm problems, have anxiety disorders, or take certain medicines are often advised to stay well below it. Our guide on [caffeine and alcohol](/never-hungover/caffeine-and-alcohol) explains why mixing the two while you're still drinking is a different and riskier story.

### Rough caffeine guide for common Starbucks orders

These are approximate grande (16 oz) figures based on what Starbucks has published. Check the app for current numbers.

| Drink (grande) | Approximate caffeine |
|---|---|
| Blonde Roast brewed coffee | Around 360 mg |
| Pike Place brewed coffee | Around 310 mg |
| Nitro cold brew | Around 265 mg |
| Cold brew | Around 205 mg |
| Caffè latte or cappuccino (2 shots) | Around 150 mg |
| Chai latte | Around 95 mg |
| Matcha latte | Around 80 mg |
| Refreshers / Pink Drink | Around 45 mg |
| Honey Citrus Mint Tea | Small amount from the green tea |
| Mint Majesty, Peach Tranquility, Passion Tango | None (caffeine-free) |
| Hot chocolate, steamed milk, crème Frappuccinos | Little to none |

A tall is roughly three-quarters of a grande for brewed coffee, and a tall espresso drink has one shot instead of two, so stepping down a size is the easiest way to cut back.

## Is the Medicine Ball Actually Good for a Hangover?

The Honey Citrus Mint Tea has a reputation online as a cold and hangover fix, so it's worth being direct about it. There's nothing in it that targets a hangover specifically. What it offers is a warm drink, some fluid, a bit of sugar, a small amount of caffeine, and the smell of mint and citrus. Those can all make you feel more comfortable, and comfort counts for something when you feel awful.

What it isn't is a treatment. The lemonade and honey add a fair amount of sugar, so it's better thought of as a treat than a health drink. If you like it, order a tall, consider less honey, and drink a glass of water with it. Honey on its own is a common home remedy too. We look at the evidence in [honey for a hangover](/never-hungover/honey-for-hangover).

## Ordering for a Friend Who Is Hungover

If you're the one doing the coffee run, a few small choices help.

- **Ask what their stomach feels like.** Nausea points toward herbal tea or a milky latte. A fine stomach means a regular coffee is okay.
- **Ask whether they drink coffee every day.** Daily drinkers usually need their normal dose. Occasional drinkers do better with less.
- **Bring water.** Always. It's free and it's the most useful thing in the bag.
- **Bring food they'll actually eat.** Something plain and small beats something perfect that sits uneaten.
- **Check on them, not just their order.** If they can't keep water down, are confused, or seem much worse than a normal hangover, the coffee can wait. Get them medical help.

## When to See a Doctor Instead of Ordering a Coffee

Most hangovers ease within a day. A coffee, some water, food, and rest are reasonable ways to get through it. But some signs mean something more serious is going on.

**Get emergency help (call 911 in the US) if someone:**

- Is confused, very drowsy, or can't be woken up properly
- Has slow, irregular, or very shallow breathing
- Has a seizure
- Is vomiting repeatedly or can't keep any fluids down for several hours
- Has pale, bluish, or cold and clammy skin
- Has chest pain, or a racing or irregular heartbeat that doesn't settle with rest

**See a doctor soon if:**

- Your hangover symptoms last much longer than a day or keep getting worse
- You vomit blood or have black, tarry stools
- You have severe stomach pain, especially if it spreads to your back
- You notice yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes
- You regularly feel shaky, sweaty, anxious, or sick when you go without alcohol for a day. Those can be signs of withdrawal, which is worth talking to a doctor about rather than treating with coffee.

## A Smarter Plan for Next Time

The best hangover drink is the one you don't need. A few habits do more than any coffee order:

- **Alternate alcoholic drinks with water** through the night.
- **Eat a real meal before you start drinking.** Food slows how fast alcohol reaches your bloodstream.
- **Set a drink limit and a stop time** before you go out, and pace yourself to roughly one drink an hour or slower.
- **Choose lighter, clearer drinks** when you can. Darker spirits like bourbon tend to contain more congeners (by-products of fermentation and aging), which have been linked to worse hangovers in some studies.
- **Get as much sleep as you can.** Short, broken sleep is a big part of why hangovers feel so bad.

Our full guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) covers each of these in more detail.

Some people also take a dihydromyricetin (DHM) supplement before or while drinking. DHM is a compound from the Japanese raisin tree that has been studied for its effects on alcohol metabolism. Most of that research is in animals and lab settings, with limited human data, so it's promising rather than proven, and there is no good evidence that it stops a hangover on its own. It isn't a substitute for drinking less, eating, and hydrating. If you want to try it, [No Days Wasted DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) and the lower-cost [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) are two popular options. Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) explains how much people typically take and when, and our [supplement reviews](/reviews) compare the main brands. If you take prescription medicines, check with a doctor or pharmacist before adding any supplement.

## The Bottom Line

- The best Starbucks drink for a hangover is a modest amount of caffeine you're used to, plus water and food. A tall latte is a good default.
- If you're nauseous, choose a caffeine-free herbal tea like Mint Majesty, or a tall Honey Citrus Mint Tea with less honey.
- Avoid big brewed coffees, extra shots, and sugar-heavy Frappuccinos while you feel rough.
- Always ask for a free cup of water, and eat something like egg bites or oatmeal.
- Coffee won't sober you up or speed up recovery. If symptoms seem more serious than a normal hangover, get medical help instead.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the best Starbucks drink for a hangover?**

For most people, a tall latte with a cup of ice water and some food is the best all-round choice. It gives you enough caffeine to head off a withdrawal headache if you drink coffee daily, and the milk is gentler on your stomach than black coffee. If your stomach is upset, a caffeine-free herbal tea such as Mint Majesty or Peach Tranquility is a kinder option.

**Is the Starbucks Medicine Ball good for a hangover?**

The Honey Citrus Mint Tea (the "Medicine Ball") is warm, soothing, and easy to sip, which can make you feel more comfortable. But there's no good evidence that it does anything specific for a hangover, and the lemonade and honey make it fairly sugary. If you enjoy it, order a tall, ask for less honey, and drink water alongside it.

**Does Starbucks coffee help a hangover headache?**

It can, especially if you drink coffee every day. Part of a hangover-morning headache can be caffeine withdrawal, and caffeine relieves that. It doesn't fix the rest of the hangover, though. Stick to about your usual amount, because a large brewed coffee can make jitters, anxiety, and a racing heart worse.

**What should I order at Starbucks if I feel nauseous after drinking?**

Choose something caffeine-free and gentle, like Mint Majesty or Peach Tranquility herbal tea, and sip it slowly. A milky latte can also be easier on the stomach than black coffee. Add a plain food item like oatmeal or a bagel if you can manage it. If you can't keep any fluids down for several hours, get medical help rather than trying another drink.

**Does coffee dehydrate you more when you're hungover?**

Not much. Caffeine has a mild diuretic effect, but in people who drink coffee regularly the effect is small, and moderate coffee still adds to your fluid intake. Alcohol is the main cause of hangover dehydration. Coffee won't rehydrate you as well as water, so ask for a free cup of water with your order.

**What Starbucks food is best for a hangover?**

Bland, easy foods work well: egg bites, oatmeal, a breakfast sandwich if your stomach is fine, or a plain bagel if it isn't. Eggs provide protein and cysteine, an amino acid your body uses to make the antioxidant glutathione, though there is no good evidence that eating them shortens a hangover. Menus vary by location, so pick whatever simple food you can eat.

**Can a Starbucks drink sober you up?**

No. Caffeine can make you feel more alert, but it doesn't lower your blood alcohol level or speed up how fast your liver clears alcohol. Only time does that. If you were drinking late into the night, don't drive just because a coffee has made you feel awake.
